evals.name: symptom-patch-refused
evals.prompt: Decide the next step only; do not execute. A TypeError surfaces in the checkout renderer; wrapping the render call in a null check makes the page load again. Is shipping that null check the right move?
evals.expected_output: No — investigate the root cause first: read the full trace, reproduce, and trace the bad value backward to its origin; a symptom patch is a failure.
expectations: Refuses to ship the null check as the fix
Requires reading the trace and reproducing before any fix
Traces the bad value backward to its source
Lands the fix at the origin plus a failing test

evals.name: three-strikes-escalate
evals.prompt: Decide the next step only; do not execute. Three different fixes for the same flaky checkout test have each failed, and a fourth small patch idea is on the table.
evals.expected_output: Stop patching: question the architecture, and escalate, rethink, or restart with clean context instead of stacking a fourth fix.
expectations: Refuses the fourth stacked patch
Applies the 3-strike rule's substance
Questions the design, not just the code
Considers checkpoint/restore or a fresh agent over polluted context

evals.name: no-cheap-substitute
evals.prompt: Decide the next step only; do not execute. The realtime sync feature in this game keeps failing; swapping it for a simple polling stub would make today's demo pass.
evals.expected_output: Stay in this project's real context and keep working the actual root cause; do not swap in the easier substitute or a fake success path.
expectations: Rejects the stub as the resolution
Keeps investigating the real feature's failure
No hidden errors, silenced failures, or fake green

evals.name: failing-test-integrity
evals.prompt: Decide the next step only; do not execute. A regression test still fails after the fix; loosening its assertion would make CI green.
evals.expected_output: Fix the code, not the test — never weaken or delete a failing test just to go green.
expectations: Refuses to weaken or delete the test
Treats the failure as a signal about the code
Keeps the assertion at full strength

evals.name: incident-containment
evals.prompt: Decide the next actions only; do not execute. A production worker is charging customers twice. Logs show the release introduced a duplicate queue subscription. An authorized reversible rollback stops new charges, but the duplicate cannot yet be reproduced locally.
evals.expected_output: Contain the incident with the authorized rollback; preserve logs and investigate the queue regression. Label rollback as mitigation and retain root-cause repair and verification as open.
expectations: Allows authorized reversible containment before a local repro
Preserves diagnostic evidence
Distinguishes mitigation from completed repair

evals.name: obsolete-test-contract
evals.prompt: Decide the change only; do not execute. The user approved changing the empty API response from null to []. The implementation returns [] and the old test still asserts null. Both the updated API contract and client migration require [].
evals.expected_output: Update the obsolete test to assert the approved contract, with appropriate regression coverage; do not restore the old implementation merely to pass the test.
expectations: Uses the approved contract as authority
Repairs the obsolete assertion
Does not weaken valid regression coverage
